evals.name: rewrite-release-note
evals.prompt: Our marketing intern drafted release-note.md for Relay 2.4.1 and it reads like a bot wrote it. Rewrite it so a person on the team could have written it. Keep every number, name, date, link, and the customer quote exactly as they are. Write the result to output.md.
evals.expected_output: A release note with the same facts, the customer quote verbatim, no em dashes, no curly quotes, sentence-case headings, no emoji, no AI vocabulary, and no chatbot closer. Length near the original, not a staccato summary.
verbatim: Relay is not just a tool — it’s the backbone of how our team collaborates, and 2.4 was a game-changer.
assertions: No em dashes or spaced en dashes outside quoted text (rule 13)
No curly quotes outside quoted text (rule 19)
Headings are sentence case (rule 17)
No emoji (rule 18)
No AI vocabulary, puffery, or metaphor nouns (rules 1, 4, 7, 8, 26, 31)
No filler phrases or 'not just X but Y' (rules 9, 23)
No chatbot or sycophantic phrases (rules 20, 22)
No bullet or paragraph opens with a bold label and a colon (rule 16)
No knowing asides (rule 34, proxy: a phrase list from iteration 1)
Every fact survives
Quoted text survives as written (Guards)
Length between 55% and 130% of the input
Not over-corrected: under 15% fragments, no 'Not X.' closers (Guards)

evals.name: slack-incident-message
evals.prompt: Write a Slack message from me to the #relay-eng channel about this morning's incident. Facts: the sync API returned 503 from 09:12 to 09:41 UTC on 2026-09-20; cause was the batched writer from 2.4.1 holding a table lock on `workspace_files` during a 2.1 TB import for workspace ws_8f3k; 41 workspaces saw failed syncs, none lost data; Marta rolled back the writer at 09:38 and the fix is in PR #1462, which caps a batch at 5000 rows. Keep it under 200 words. Save it as message.md.
evals.expected_output: A message under 200 words with every fact, no chatbot phrases, no em dashes, no emoji, and no title-case headings. Reads like a person, not a status page.
